emails.subject: {{first_name}}, quick question about SDR coverage
emails.body:
{{first_name}}, what happens to your pipeline when one of your SDRs goes on parental leave for 3 months?

Most sales leaders we talk to say they just split the book across the team. Then connect rates drop for everyone.

We've helped a few mid-market teams maintain full pipeline coverage during similar gaps. Their AEs didn't even notice the difference.

Worth a quick chat about how they set that up?

{{first_name}}, the reason I ask is because 70% of the pipeline from that territory usually just goes dark during leave. And training someone new for a 4-month window doesn't pencil out.

We've been the bridge for a few teams in similar spots. Only get paid when meetings are actually qualified.

Would it help to hear how they handled it?

emails.subject: {{first_name}}, something that surprised us
emails.body:
{{first_name}}, one thing that surprised us working with teams your size: the pipeline gap from a single SDR on leave usually shows up 6-8 weeks later, not immediately.

By the time most leaders react, they've already lost a quarter's worth of coverage.

Curious, do you have a playbook for when that happens, or is it more of a figure-it-out-when-it-comes situation?

{{first_name}}, I know there's about {{employee_count}} people over at {{company_name}} and maybe SDR coverage isn't something you're thinking about right now. Should I reach out to {{other_contact_name}} instead given their role?
